rows.question: q3
rows.quote: A deterministic kernel and compiler turn a loadout graph into a bounded program and an authority envelope that is checked on every decision, and a typed reactor folds durable events into replayable state. | The Repo Gardener plus Seiri scenario runs end to end from a JSONL event log, refuses deletion structurally and verifies its candidates with a separate fake verifier.
rows.answer:
The source prepares version v0.73.1. What runs today:
- A deterministic kernel and compiler turn a loadout graph into a bounded program, with an authority envelope checked on every decision. A typed reactor folds durable events into state that can be replayed.
- The Repo Gardener + Seiri scenario runs end to end from a JSONL event log. It refuses deletion structurally and has a separate fake verifier check its candidates.
- Disposable worker episodes on Claude Code and Codex have changed a synthetic module in isolated worktrees, passed its host test and committed, with a blinded verifier judging the change.
- The `publish` and `vertical` commands can open a pull request under an operator grant, and run the loop from a filed issue through review triage. So far this has only happened in recorded scratch proofs.
- A resident host dispatches bounded episodes and holds further dispatch when a mission check finds drift. It is not an installed service, and it has no measured payoff curve.
- A browser evidence adapter collects screenshot, DOM, network and console witnesses.
- An `intent` command files draft work orders.
- An actor board, a text console and a live console are available.
- The repository itself runs on this same machinery.
rows.reason: The answer carries at least five keyed facts: the deterministic kernel and compiler with the authority envelope, the Repo Gardener plus Seiri scenario replayed from an event log, the Claude and Codex worker episodes in isolated worktrees with a separate verifier, the resident host with the mission check holding dispatch, and the actor board and text console. The two quotes support the first two facts.
